newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan's Bashir says no concern over Mahdi exile.
newsitem.headline: Sudan's Bashir says no concern over Mahdi exile.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir said his government was not frightened by the flight of opposition leader and former prime minister Sadeq al-Mahdi to Eritrea, where the armed opposition is based.

The Sudanese news agency SUNA on Thursday quoted Bashir as saying Mahdi's "joining of the so-called opposition would not frighten the revolution and would not affect its adherence to its civilisational orientation (Islamic law)".
Bashir was speaking in Khartoum to 5,000 universtiy student recruits of the Popular Defence Force, which was set up in 1989 to help government troops in their civil war against southern rebels.

Mahdi appeared at a news conference in Asmara on Wednesday and said he slipped out of Khartoum last Thursday. He said he wanted "a united effort against the regime in Khartoum, with a minimum of bloodshed."

Bashir overthrew Mahdi's democratically elected government in a bloodless coup in 1989. Since then, Mahdi -- the head of Sudan's largest party Umma and spiritual leader of the Ansar or Mahdist movement, has been arrested several times.
His flight from Khartoum is a major coup for the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), the broad opposition coalition that has started attacking Sudan from Eritrean territory.
Bashir said the coming together of the opposition abroad would not have any effect on Sudan.

He said the attempt by Mahdi and other opposition leaders to come to power in Sudan under the command of rebel leader John Garang and Eritrean President Isayas Afewerki was motivated by "private interests and would never halt the Sudanese Islamic march".
